dialog.nativeNote: This provider also supports native sign-in. Signing in from the desktop depends on the core's login API (PRD 0001, RF2); for now, sign in with the TUI and the account will appear here.

settings.title: Settings
settings.motion.label: Animations
settings.motion.help: System follows the operating system's reduced-motion preference.
settings.folder.title: Themes and languages folder
settings.folder.help: Themes (.css) and languages (.json) placed in this folder are loaded at startup.
settings.folder.env: Set by the CUOTAI_USER_DIR variable; the choice here only applies once it is removed.
settings.config.title: Accounts file
settings.config.help: cuotai.toml used by the app. Pick the same file as the TUI to see the same accounts; nothing is copied or merged.
config.other: The TUI last used {tui}, this app uses {app}: accounts and model caches are separate. To align, choose the same file in Settings › Accounts file.
settings.config.env: Set by the CUOTAI_CONFIG variable; a choice made here only applies after removing it.
settings.config.error.unwritable: Accounts were reloaded, but the choice could not be saved.
settings.config.error.env_locked: The CUOTAI_CONFIG variable is set and takes priority.
settings.error.invalid_path: Invalid folder: use an absolute path and do not pick the disk root.
settings.error.not_dir: The chosen path is not a folder.
settings.error.unwritable: Could not create or write to that folder.
settings.error.env_locked: The CUOTAI_USER_DIR variable is set and takes priority.
settings.error.invalid_history_days: Keep the history from 7 to 365 days.
settings.error.invalid_notify: Pick one of the lead times and filters offered.
settings.error.invalid_threshold: Each threshold must be a whole number from 10 to 99%.
settings.notify.title: Notifications
settings.notify.help: A system notice when a quota resets, per the time the provider reported. Sent by the app while it runs (also hidden in the tray), once per reset; no extra query is made, the new balance shows on the next refresh.
settings.notify.denied: The system did not allow notifications from Cuotai, so the option stays off.
settings.notify.system: Open the system settings → Notifications, allow Cuotai and turn the option on again. Use “Send test notification” to check.
settings.notify.whenHelp: Windows of 5 hours, a day, a week or a month; rate limits and balances never notify.
settings.alerts.help: A system notice when a quota with a limit reaches a threshold of use, once per threshold and window; also hidden in the tray, never with the app closed and with no extra query. Balances, spend and rate limits never alert.
settings.alerts.thresholdsHelp: Share of the quota used, from {min} to {max}%. Click a threshold to remove it.
settings.alerts.recovery: Notify recovery in the next window
settings.notify.accounts: Each account has a bell on its card and in its details that turns its reset notices and usage alerts on or off; in the details, each quota can also mute its own alerts. The choices are saved per provider and account name: renaming the account turns them back on.
settings.notify.testSent: Test notification sent. If it did not appear, allow Cuotai in the system notification settings.
settings.notify.testFailed: The test notification could not be sent.
notify.test.title: Cuotai: test notification
notify.test.body: Cuotai notices will look like this.
account.reorder: Drag to reorder (or use the arrow keys)
sort.label: Sort

tray.allOkTitle.one: {count} account up to date with no alerts.
tray.allOkTitle.other: {count} accounts up to date with no alerts.

card.binding.title: Most restrictive limit right now
settings.group.help: Accounts with a used-up quota move to a collapsible group with their return time. Display only: the manual order inside each group and the order saved in the file stay as they are.
settings.pace.help: Compares what was used with a steady pace until the reset and says whether it lasts. A linear estimate, not a promise; windows that just opened show nothing.
settings.history.title: History
settings.history.help: Each successful reading is recorded on this computer only (numbers and windows, never credentials or provider text). Older samples are thinned to one per hour after 7 days and the file stays under 64 MiB.
settings.history.eraseAll: Erase the whole measurement history on this computer, for every configuration? This cannot be undone.
settings.history.eraseOne: Erase the measurement history of {account}? This cannot be undone.
settings.history.recordHelp: Off: nothing new is recorded, and what was already recorded stays (kept for the days below) until you erase it. Applies to this app; the terminal and the command line still record.
settings.history.size: On disk: {size} (the whole history on this computer).
trend.title: History
trend.range.label: Period
trend.off: Recording is off (Settings → History): the chart shows what was recorded before.
trend.empty.day: No reading of this account was recorded in the last 24 hours.
trend.empty.week: No reading of this account was recorded in the last 7 days.
trend.empty.month: No reading of this account was recorded in the last 30 days.
trend.emptyHelp: Each successful reading is recorded on this computer; the chart fills in from the next ones.
trend.noUsed: No measured use in this period.
card.pace.estimate: Linear estimate from the use so far; it may change.
settings.order.title: Account order
settings.order.help: Shows the accounts closest to their limit first. The manual order (drag and drop, shared with the TUI) stays saved and returns when this is off.
dialog.copyFailed: Could not copy; select the text and copy it manually.
dialog.login.codePlaceholder: Paste the code shown by the provider
dialog.login.browserUnavailable: Could not open the browser; open the URL above manually.
dialog.login.authorized: Signed in; account parameters were filled in automatically.
dialog.login.validating: Validating the code in the pending session…
dialog.login.profileRequired: Enter a profile name for `bl` (letters, numbers, '-' or '_').
dialog.login.clientIdRequired: Enter the client_id of YOUR registered OAuth application.
dialog.login.doneHint: Signed in for this session. Saving writes the credential to the vault and the account to the file.
dialog.reg.clientIdHelp: OAuth application you registered with the provider.
dialog.reg.secretEnvHelp: Enter only the NAME of the environment variable, never its value.
dialog.reg.tenantHelp: Leave empty to use the provider default.
dialog.save.loginRunning: Sign-in in progress; finish or cancel it before saving.
dialog.save.needLogin: Finish signing in before saving (or go back to the manual credential).
dialog.save.profileChanged: The profile changed after sign-in; sign in again before saving.
dialog.conflict.reloaded: File reloaded from disk; review and save again when ready.
dialog.external.title: Configuration changed on disk
dialog.external.body: The configuration file changed outside the app. Reloading picks up the latest version; continuing edits against the old snapshot will likely require a reload before the next save.
dialog.login.nameFirst: Enter the account name before signing in.
dialog.deleteBodyVault: {label} has a credential saved in the system vault. Delete it as well?
delete.purged: Account removed and its credential deleted from the vault.
delete.kept: Account removed; the credential stays in the vault.
delete.keptShared: Account removed; the credential was kept because account {other} also uses it.
delete.partial: Account removed from the file, but its credential was NOT deleted from the vault: {message}
delete.retry: Try to delete the credential now
settings.refresh.title: Refresh
settings.refresh.help: Global interval between queries. Accounts with their own interval do not change; providers billed per query have a higher minimum.
settings.refresh.label: Global interval (seconds)
models.title: Models
models.search: Search model by ID or name
models.empty: The provider returned no models for this credential.
models.gone: The account changed or was removed; the previous result was discarded.
models.pick: Browse models of a configured account of this provider
models.saveFirst: No account of this provider is configured; save the account and open its details to query.
models.demo: Browser demo: the model catalog is only queried in the desktop app.
about.libraries.help: Cuotai is built on open source projects maintained by their communities. Thanks to everyone who builds them. Logos are trademarks of their respective owners.
about.role.build.note: Used only while compiling the app.
about.role.asset.note: Icons shipped with the desktop app.
about.role.theme.note: Open palettes the built-in themes follow.
about.brazil: Special thanks: projects created by Brazilians
about.brazil.note: Open source software made in Brazil that shapes Cuotai.
about.role.reference.note: Logic and contracts adapted to Rust; the original code is not run.
incident.title: Provider status
incident.openFailed: Could not open the status page.
incident.stale: The latest status query failed; this is the previous reading.
settings.privacy.title: Privacy
settings.status.on: Check the providers' public status pages
settings.status.help: Off by default. When on, Cuotai makes public requests to the status pages of the providers you configured, at most once every 5 minutes per page, without credentials, cookies or account data. Those sites can see your IP address and that you use the provider. Incidents appear on the cards and on the tray icon.
settings.status.none: None of your configured providers has a verified status page; nothing would be queried.
settings.serve.title: Integration
settings.serve.help: A read-only local server lets status bars and scripts read your usage (/v1/snapshot, /v1/limits, /v1/accounts/{key}, /health) in the export v1 format. It serves this app's own readings: reading it never queries a provider.
settings.serve.on: Serve my usage on a local address
settings.serve.cuotaiOnPort: Another Cuotai server (such as cuotai --serve) is already using port {port}: stop it or choose another port here.
settings.serve.portHelp: Default {port}, from {min} to {max}. Exactly this port is used: when it is taken, the server stays off and says so.
settings.serve.token.title: Access token
settings.serve.token.on: Every request must send Authorization: Bearer <token>. The token is kept in the system vault, never in cuotai.toml, and is never shown: copy it into your client.
settings.serve.token.off: No token: any program running as you on this computer can read the server; web pages are still refused.
settings.serve.token.revokeHelp: A new token stops the old one at once. Revoking removes it from the vault, and the server answers without a token again.
settings.serve.browsersOff: Off: requests from web pages are refused and no page can read the answers.
settings.serve.privacy: It only listens on this computer (127.0.0.1) and never serves credentials. Any program running under your user can read what it serves, as with cuotai --json.
serve.banner: The local server is not serving:
